title: 32.5 A 2W 53.2%-Peak-Efficiency Multi-Core Isolated DC-DC Converter with Embedded Magnetic-Core Transformer Achieving CISPR-32 Class-B EMI Compliance and <5mV Ripple
problem: Integrated isolated DC-DC converters suffer from severe conducted EMI (150kHz-30MHz) and radiated EMI (30MHz-1GHz) due to PWM control and common-mode currents across transformer parasitic capacitance, requiring bulky filters and reducing power delivery efficiency at 1W scale.
motivation: Minimizing power supply size and cost in isolated systems demands low-noise, high-efficiency conversion without external components; this is critical for board-area-constrained and cost-sensitive applications.
method: The converter uses a symmetrical multi-core design with an embedded transformer to suppress common-mode current (electrical noise that leaks through the transformer's internal capacitance). A high-speed switching converter using pulse-width modulation (PWM—rapid on-off switching at tens of MHz) regulated by a slower feedback loop (~1 MHz) manages the voltage conversion while the transformer architecture actively reduces electromagnetic noise and output ripple. The result is less than 5mV output ripple and CISPR-32 Class-B electromagnetic compliance without external filters.
key_novelty: A multi-core isolated converter with an embedded magnetic transformer achieves electromagnetic noise suppression and efficiency in a single integrated chip.
contributions: CISPR-32 Class-B EMI compliance without external filters
Sub-5mV output ripple with integrated transformer
limitations: Abstract focuses on topology and EMI performance; power delivery capacity (1W) and specific frequency range constraints not fully discussed relative to emerging miniaturized system demands.
